subject: Information Theory
title: KL Divergence
description: A fast breakdown of KL Divergence for builders.

hook.text: You think a coin is fair. It's actually biased 70/30. How wrong are you? KL divergence tells you exactly.

buildup.text: Kullback-Leibler divergence measures the extra bits wasted when you assume the wrong distribution.

discovery.text: D(P||Q) = Σ P(x) log(P(x)/Q(x)). It's always ≥ 0 and equals zero only when P = Q.

twist.text: It's not symmetric: D(P||Q) ≠ D(Q||P). The penalty depends on which direction you're wrong.

climax.text: Machine learning uses KL divergence to measure how far a model's predictions are from reality.

quiz.question: What does KL divergence measure?
options: The extra bits from using the wrong probability distribution
